title: Domestic comfort with choice restored

captions.energy: Keeping convenience despite its restrictive cost
captions.emotions: Feeling attachment to familiar material support

meaning: Your domestic support becomes freer when considered choice distinguishes actual convenience from attachment that prevents discussion of its cost.
text: You can arrange domestic life thoughtfully: understanding a need, assessing a method and using accumulated experience. The Hermit in the physical position of Muladhara describes these actions. The Devil in energy complicates them through binding convenience for which choice gradually narrows. The Devil in emotions feels attachment and difficulty releasing the familiar. The repeated card distinguishes dependence on an arrangement from experiencing its loss. Even after noticing excessive cost, both may keep maintaining a habit because domestic support seems insufficiently real without its material confirmation.

For example, many rarely used kitchen gadgets have accumulated. Storage crowds out essentials, but release is difficult because each promised to ease shared life. **Promised usefulness does not oblige you to maintain attachment indefinitely.** You can recognise the earlier wish and check current use. Experience restores room for actual needs, while clearing a shelf need not first require convincing yourselves that wanting convenience was wrong or unworthy of attention.

The difficulty is seeking one more gadget to organise all the accumulated comfort. Keeping it becomes costlier without bringing enough. Distinguishing the useful from the untouchable offers more dependable support: an object can once have been wanted and still stop helping. Thoughtfulness restores both people’s right to choose present life without confirming every former choice through further expenditure of shared space and time.
